verified_subject: Fresh Eastern Bering Sea pollock paper, September 11th, 2026
challenge_a: Strongest framing: policy discovery and changing biological assumptions. Its falsifier can genuinely break the account. Tighten makes reinforcement learning useful to demonstrates a research use, since practical superiority over improved conventional rules remains untested. Replace removes the easy conclusion with changes the tradeoff. Preserve each comparison baseline explicitly.
challenge_c: The title A Smoother Catch Has a Cost risks conflating a smoother harvest-policy function with lower year-to-year catch variability. F12 establishes the policy is smoother, not an independently verified catch-variability statistic. Do not say the first-half problem is solved: these are different biological scenarios, not a before-and-after repair. Also lower spawning biomass is not automatically damage or unsustainability. C correctly makes that distinction in its counterpoint but its title pulls against it.
strongest_thesis_revision: A revised A: This pollock simulation demonstrates a research use for reinforcement learning: discovering harvest rules whose benefits and costs change when the assumed relationship between young fish and breeding stock changes. Alaska gains a clearer set of alternatives to investigate, not a proven best policy.
second_movement_verdict: Earned if it changes the audience judgment about biomass rather than claiming stability was fixed. Constant recruitment: higher spawning biomass with catch swings. Stock-linked recruitment: higher catches with lower spawning biomass relative to its comparison. State smoother policy only if needed; omit it if viewers could read it as demonstrated steadier annual income.
falsifiability_verdict: A factual reproduction that removes the scenario-specific tradeoffs defeats the selected descriptive thesis. Practical value remains a prospective research judgment and should be phrased accordingly.
